title: Cipla Ltd Gross Margin Analysis Shows Peer Median Proximity Across Quarters
abstract: This research note evaluates the financial performance and gross margin metrics of Cipla Ltd, a pharmaceutical manufacturer listed on the National Stock Exchange of India, as of 20 October 2026. We examined 9 quarters of filed results to understand profitability trends and compare them against 5 listed peers. The primary finding indicates that the company change was within 1.6 robust standard deviations of the peer median, which is too close to call company-specific. Revenue from operations in Q3 FY25 was Rs 7,073.0 crore, compared to Rs 6,603.8 crore a year earlier in Q3 FY24. Additional examination shows the pat margin reaches 22.3 per cent in Q3FY25 with a pat margin, peer z-score of z = 1.5, reflecting specific financial variations. Meanwhile, the gross margin changepoint in Q3FY24 reflects cost pressures affecting profitability, though this explanation was rejected because the company change remained within 1.6 robust standard deviations of the peer median. The outlook notes that the finding would be undermined if net profit margin falls to or below 0.0 per cent for 2 consecutive quarters, with the next test expected around 13 February 2027.
introduction: Cipla Ltd is a pharmaceutical manufacturer listed on the National Stock Exchange of India, as of 20 October 2026 [1]. This note focuses on gross margin, compared against 5 listed peers [1]. We aim to provide a detailed review of the financial results filed by the company across multiple reporting periods [1].
company_and_data: We examined 9 quarters of filed results to establish the revenue and margin trajectory of the enterprise [1]. Revenue from operations in Q3 FY25 was Rs 7,073.0 crore [1]. A year earlier, in Q3 FY24, it was Rs 6,603.8 crore [5]. findings: The company's change was within 1.6 robust standard deviations of the peer median, which is too close to call company-specific [1]. We observed that this metric forms the primary baseline for our comparative evaluation against the selected listed peers [1].
A finding survived the checks, confirming the robustness of the comparative peer assessment [1]. The surviving explanation held against every check applied to its strongest rivals [1].
explanations: The pat margin reaches 22.3 per cent in Q3FY25 with a pat margin, peer z-score of z = 1.5, reflecting specific financial variations, and this explanation is supported [1]. The company moved 3.7 robust standard deviations away from the median of 4 peers, so the change is specific to it [1]. The change has held for 7 quarters against an earlier average of 11.4 per cent [1].

The gross margin changepoint in Q3FY24 reflects cost pressures affecting profitability, but this explanation was rejected [1]. The company's change was within 1.6 robust standard deviations of the peer median, which is too close to call company-specific [1]. The change has held for 5 quarters against an earlier average of 64.3 per cent [1].
outlook: The finding would be undermined if net profit margin falls to or below 0.0 per cent for 2 consecutive quarters [1]. The next test is Cipla Ltd.'s next quarterly results, expected around 13 February 2027 [1].
conclusion: We conclude that the financial metrics of Cipla Ltd demonstrate distinct patterns when evaluated against peer groups [1]. The proximity of the company change to the peer median provides a clear boundary for interpreting profitability trends [1].

Future monitoring of the quarterly results will determine the persistence of these observed financial variations [1]. Analysts will observe upcoming reporting milestones to verify the continuity of these margins [1].
